items.title: [agritechinsights.com] Farmers test soil and heat-tolerant crops as drought strains fields
items.content_html:
🌾 ✏️

Farmers and researchers are adapting to drought and extreme heat with soil checks, crop trials and changes to farm work. In Poland, soil scientist Bartłomiej Glina says growers should assess soil structure, compaction and water storage before relying on irrigation. Researchers in India screened linseed varieties for late-season heat tolerance, while Romanian teams tested sweet potatoes, peanuts and cowpea as alternative crops. A global study projects that saline soils will expand by 8% across drylands by 2100 under a high-emissions scenario. Research on heat waves found that feedback between temperature, soil moisture and atmospheric pressure can increase the intensity of the most extreme events by 10%. In Senegal, workers report shorter hours in the fields as heat intensifies. In India’s Jarandi area, drought is threatening guava and sweet-lime orchards as wells and other water sources decline.

items.title: [tygodnik-rolniczy.pl] Small farms pursue saffron, seed processing and direct vegetable sales
items.content_html:
🌾 ✏️

Four farm profiles from Poland and Romania show how producers earn income from agriculture. Dorota Kaliszewska, a Polish farmer in the Lublin region, is testing saffron; Romanian grower Robert Zamisnicu cultivates vegetables and melons on 40 hectares; and Polish pumpkin-seed entrepreneur Łukasz Popielewicz relies on contract growers and processing. Filip and Magda Partyka run a 14-hectare vegetable farm and sell directly to households. Zamisnicu said an early-August hailstorm damaged about half his crop, while Kaliszewska lost some saffron bulbs to excess moisture in her first season. Popielewicz's company handled about 5,000 tonnes of pumpkin seeds last year and is targeting up to 9,000 tonnes this year, depending on the harvest.

items.title: [agfundernews.com] John Deere buys Orchard AI to add plant-level crop data
items.content_html: John Deere has acquired Orchard Robotics, which operates as Orchard AI, adding its camera-based crop monitoring and FruitScope software to the equipment maker’s precision-agriculture business. The deal, announced Nov. 19, pairs plant-level data for specialty-crop growers with Deere machinery that can act on field recommendations. Financial terms were not disclosed. The system scans trees, vines and other crops to assess fruit size, crop health and expected yield, helping growers decide when and where to thin, spray or harvest. Orchard will remain a Deere subsidiary with its existing team and products, founder and CEO Charlie Wu said. The acquisition also expands Deere’s orchard and vineyard automation portfolio.
